label: Some Technicalities
notes: Open the appendix as a toolkit rather than a detour. The chapter supplies the smoothness and support conventions that make the variational arguments legal on domains with edges, collars, and compactly supported perturbations. Tell learners that these tools are small, but they decide whether a formal variation is admissible.

label: Closed Domains Need Smooth Extensions
notes: Stress the local extension test. A map on a closed domain is treated as smooth when it is the restriction of a smooth map nearby. That convention lets calculus operate at boundary points without inventing one-sided differential rules.

label: Support Records Where A Variation Acts
notes: Use support as a bookkeeping device for variations. If the support stays away from the boundary, integration by parts loses its boundary term. That is exactly why compact support appears so often in variational derivations.

label: Bump Functions Localize Geometry
notes: A bump function is a smooth switch. It is zero outside a chosen region, one where the experiment should happen, and smooth through the transition. The point is not the formula, but the ability to localize a variation without tearing differentiability.

label: Cutoffs Make Legal Test Fields
notes: Explain the workflow: start with the field one wants, multiply by a cutoff, and obtain an admissible compactly supported field. Then shrink the cutoff region to test the local equation. This is how a global variation argument turns into a pointwise Euler-Lagrange condition without abusing the boundary.

label: Collars And Boundaries
notes: Collar coordinates turn a boundary into a product direction. This makes it clear which variable is tangential and which is normal to the edge, so support and extension statements become drawable rather than abstract. Use this as the visual bridge between domain language and the boundary terms seen in integration by parts.

label: Pitfalls
notes: Name the common mistakes explicitly. Continuity is not smoothness, support is not the same as the region where a formula is visually large, and a cutoff that is sharp in a plot may fail to be smooth.

label: Takeaways
notes: End by tying the appendix back to the main course. These technical conventions are the permissions system for local variation, integration by parts, and boundary-aware geometric computation. The appendix earns its keep whenever a proof says choose a smooth compactly supported perturbation.
